audit.whatIsWrong: content.early instructs 'Watch his mana — a pooling Vlad has to commit to it'. Vladimir has no mana.
audit.why: His resource is Crimson Rush and every ability in his kit costs zero: Transfusion 0, Sanguine Pool 0, Hemoplague 0. Tides of Blood is paid for in health, not mana. So the entry hands the player a resource bar to track that does not exist, and in doing so it misses the tell that does. Crimson Rush matters enormously: when it is full, Transfusion gets massively increased damage and healing for a brief window. That full bar is the actual 'he is about to hurt you' signal in this lane, and it is nowhere in either layer.
audit.corrected: Vladimir is manaless. Watch Crimson Rush instead — a full bar means his next Transfusion hits and heals for far more.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (resource: Crimson Rush; Q/W/E/R all cost 0)
champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (Q Transfusion: 'When Vladimir's resource is full, Transfusion will benefit from massively increased damage and healing for a brief time')

audit.whatIsWrong: Three content strings credit Vladimir's sustain to a 'passive heal': late 'his Q drain and passive heal out-sustain everything', wants.foe[1] 'Sustain through your Q poke with his passive heal and Q drain', whys[3] 'his Q drain and passive heal claw back your chip'. Crimson Pact does not heal.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts bonus health into ability power and ability power into bonus health. It is a stat-conversion passive with no healing component whatsoever — his healing is Transfusion (Q) and Hemoplague (R). The mislabel costs the player the single most useful fact about scaling into Vladimir: because every AP item silently also gives him health, he gets tankier as he gets more dangerous, which is precisely why the entry's own late-game section says he out-scales her. Naming it 'passive heal' hides the mechanism behind the scaling warning.
audit.corrected: His heals are Transfusion (Q) and Hemoplague (R). Crimson Pact (P) turns his AP into bonus health, which is why he gets bulky while building damage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (P Crimson Pact: 'Every 30 points of bonus Health gives Vladimir 1 Ability Power and every 1 point of Ability Power gives Vladimir 1.6 bonus Health'; flags: none)
champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (Q flags: heal; R flags: heal, zone)

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].t reads 'Reflect Sanguine Pool back the moment he commits'.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is a self-cast untargetable transformation — 'Vladimir sinks into a pool of blood, becoming untargetable for 2 seconds'. There is nothing travelling toward Mel to reflect. This is the same template defect I found on the Swain entry ('Reflect Demonic Ascension back the moment he commits'), so it looks systemic rather than specific to this matchup. The instruction is actively harmful: it tells the player to hold and then spend a 38-second Rebuttal at the exact moment Vladimir has become immune to everything, wasting her defensive layer on a non-event and leaving her naked for the follow-up.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool cannot be reflected. Rebuttal's value here is its damage-prevention, best spent on Hemoplague's delayed detonation.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (W Sanguine Pool flags: slow, untargetable; self-cast)
champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W Rebuttal: reflects enemy projectiles, prevents her from taking damage, grants movement speed)

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says 'My W, Rebuttal, is gold here too — it eats his E poke projectile and fires it back as my damage, so raise the barrier when he winds up his pool-of-blood throw.'
audit.why: Two problems in one sentence. Tides of Blood is not a projectile — Riot's text has it as a charged reservoir 'released, deals damage in the area around him', and its derived flags are slow and zone with no projectile flag. And 'pool-of-blood throw' merges Tides of Blood (E) with Sanguine Pool (W), which are different abilities doing different things. Vladimir in fact carries no projectile-flagged ability at all, so the reflect half of Rebuttal has no target in this matchup. What Rebuttal does still do here is prevent damage outright and grant movement speed, and there is an ideal moment for that: Hemoplague sits on the ground and detonates after a delay, and it amplifies all damage taken in the meantime.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal's damage-prevention is the tool here, not the reflect — hold it for Hemoplague's delayed detonation rather than for his E.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (E Tides of Blood flags: slow, zone — no projectile; W Sanguine Pool is a separate ability)
champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (R Hemoplague: 'Affected enemies take increased damage for the duration. After a few seconds, Hemoplague deals magic damage')

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool is the focus ability, the win condition and the tracked cooldown in both layers, and its duration and cooldown appear nowhere. content.early even reasons about it being 'still too low-rank and high-cooldown to save him every time' without giving the number.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16 with a 2 second untargetable window. Twenty-eight seconds at rank 1 is enormous — nearly three Solar Snares, since Mel's E is 11s at rank 1 — and it is the entire justification for the entry's correct advice to bait the pool with a fake step-up. Stating it turns a vague instruction into arithmetic the player can act on. The 2 second duration also matters: it tells her how long to wait before re-committing rather than dumping into the immunity.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and lasts 2 seconds. Your snare is 11s — you get roughly two roots per pool early.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t all say Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26 — 38 seconds at rank 1, below which it never goes under 26. Understating it by half is worst here of anywhere in my slice, because the same entry tells the player to spend W on a Sanguine Pool she cannot reflect.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and report[0].t say 'Poke mirror you usually win — your reflect makes his best spell a liability'. The win rate is 45.45% and his best spell is not reflectable.
audit.why: Wrong on both halves. The headline overclaims the lane against the recorded data, and it credits the win to a reflect interaction that does not exist in this matchup. The content layer is honest about the shape of the lane — 'this is where the lane gets away from me, and I have to be honest about it' — so the full layer's headline is contradicting its own body text as well as the number.
audit.corrected: Frame the lane by its real clock: Mel's windows are levels 2 through first item, and the pool is what she has to bait to use them.
sources: champ-data/content/mel.js (late: 'This is where the lane gets away from me')

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names Vladimir's sustain as the losing condition in four strings and never mentions Grievous Wounds. Only the full layer's Itemization line carries it.
audit.why: Transfusion is a zero-cost heal on 4.6s at rank 5 and Hemoplague heals him per champion hit. The entry's whole late-game thesis is that his sustain out-paces Mel's chip, which makes anti-heal the single most load-bearing item decision in the matchup — and a player reading the content panel never sees it mentioned.
audit.corrected: Put the Grievous Wounds call in the content layer where the sustain problem is described.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay mine on paper — my Q ranks up, Overwhelm accumulates off repeated pokes, and at 6 Golden Eclipse (R) turns those stacks into a real burst threat from range. Bait the W out first with poke pressure, then chain E-root into Q into R while it's down. My W, Rebuttal, is gold here too — it eats his E poke projectile and fires it back as my damage, so raise the barrier when he winds up his pool-of-blood throw.

edits.before: Vlad is one of the weakest level-1s in the game, but my early presence is real and I can punish him. Levels 2-3 are my window: once Solar Snare (E) is up I root him the second he steps into the wave to last-hit, then Radiant Volley (Q) chunks him and stacks Overwhelm while his Sanguine Pool (W) is still too low-rank and high-cooldown to save him every time. Watch his mana — a pooling Vlad has to commit to it, so bait the pool with a fake step-up, then land the real E-Q. Don't dump everything into a Vlad who's already pooled; the untargetable window eats my root and my stacks for free.

edits.before: This is where the lane gets away from me, and I have to be honest about it. Vlad is a hard scaler — once he has two AP items his Q drain and passive heal out-sustain everything my poke does, and Sanguine Pool dodges every targeted thing I own including the R execute. My infinitely-scaling Overwhelm passive keeps me relevant, but a full-build Vlad kites my dash-less, one-CC body and bursts me in the teamfight the moment I'm caught. So I have to cash in my level 2-6 and first-item windows hard, end the lane before his second item, and late-game stop trying to solo him — group, use Solar Snare to peel for myself, and let my team answer the unkillable AP threat.
edits.after: This is where the lane gets away from me, and I have to be honest about it. Vlad is a hard scaler — Crimson Pact turns every point of his AP into bonus health, so each damage item also makes him bulkier, and without Grievous Wounds his Transfusion out-sustains my poke. Sanguine Pool dodges every targeted thing I own including the R execute. My Overwhelm passive keeps me relevant, but a full-build Vlad kites my dash-less, one-CC body. So cash in my level 2-6 and first-item windows hard, end the lane before his second item, and late-game stop trying to solo him — group, peel with Solar Snare, and let my team answer him.

notes: SYSTEMIC TEMPLATE BUG, worth a global grep: dosFull[1].t here read 'Reflect Sanguine Pool back the moment he commits', and the Swain entry in my slice read 'Reflect Demonic Ascension back the moment he commits'. Both are self-cast, non-projectile abilities that Rebuttal cannot touch. The pattern looks like 'Reflect <focus ability> back the moment he commits' being auto-filled from the focus field regardless of whether the ability is a projectile. If that generator ran across all 71 Mel entries, every matchup whose focus ability is not a projectile now carries a false and dangerous instruction. I only audited my slice, so I cannot say how many are affected — but this is the highest-leverage thing in my report. Vladimir carries no projectile-flagged ability at all (Q targeted, W self-cast untargetable, E a zone around him, R a ground zone), so Rebuttal's reflect half has nothing to work with in this matchup. Per the relevance rule I did not write that as a negative anywhere; instead I redirected the W advice to what the ability genuinely still does — Riot's text says it 'prevents her from taking damage' and grants movement speed — and pointed it at Hemoplague's delayed detonation, which is the one clearly-timed damage event in his kit and which also amplifies incoming damage while it sits. content.mid also called Tides of Blood a 'projectile' and then described it as a 'pool-of-blood throw', conflating E with W. Both halves are wrong; E is a charged zone released around him. SUSPECTNAMES: both flags on this matchup are false positives. 'But Sanguine Pool' (distance 4) is the leading 'But ' and 'Solar Snare's' (distance 2) is the possessive apostrophe. The ability names in this entry's content layer are actually correct throughout — it is one of the better-named entries in the slice. Left alone: the phase chart and the EVEN 5.5/10 rating. 45.45% on 11 games with full.phases reading Mel, Mel, Mel, Skill, Skill, Skill, Vladimir against content.win's Skill, Mel, Mel, Skill, Mel, Skill, Vladimir is close enough that I had no basis to move it.
